assertions.text: The response identifies at least one statement in the report's profile section as applicable to almost anyone, rather than specific to Elaine.
The response points out that the report's claim that detail and process work drain Elaine is contradicted by her performance reviews or her own intake answers.
The response disputes the report's claim that Elaine can expect UX offers within three to six months of the bootcamp, on grounds of the entry-level UX market or her lack of any design record.
The response states that the report never engages with Elaine's financial situation.
The response calculates from Elaine's own figures how long her money lasts, or what remains after the £8,900 bootcamp fee.
The response identifies that at least one recommended path conflicts with Elaine's stated twice-weekly care for her mother or her no-nights-away constraint.
The response criticises the report for ending without recommending or ranking any of the three paths, treating that as a failing rather than a virtue.
The response points out that the report's proposed next steps ask Elaine to spend or commit before any path has been tested.
The response commits to a view on which direction Elaine's record best supports, or proposes a specific better-supported alternative, instead of treating the three paths as equally viable.
The response cites at least one specific item from Elaine's work history or performance reviews as contradicting a claim the report makes about her.
The response gives Elaine at least one concrete action for the coming month that costs nothing or nearly nothing.
The response advises Elaine not to act on the report as written.
